literal: "At that there was loud laughter and Jigao could speak no more.
idiomatic: At that they laughed aloud and Jigao could say no more.

literal: At the beginning of Daning he also served as Regular Attendant and chief envoy on the mission to Chen.
idiomatic: At the start of Daning he also served as Regular Attendant and chief envoy to Chen.

literal: At the end of Tiantong he revised the national history.
idiomatic: At the end of Tiantong he revised the national history.

literal: Soon he was made Unimpeded Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Unimpeded Regular Attendant.

literal: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Yingzhou.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously Inspector of Yingzhou.

literal: His son Bo held court appointment and attended at the Forest of Literature.
idiomatic: His son Bo held court appointment and attended at the Forest of Literature.

literal: Hao's younger brother Ye, styled Jiyan, died as Administrator of Cangzhou.
idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Ye, styled Jiyan, died as Administrator of Cangzhou.

literal: Feng Yi, styled Chude, was a man of Mao in Bohai.
idiomatic: Feng Yi, styled Chude, was from Mao in Bohai.

literal: His great-grandfather Shi was Jin Colonel for the Eastern Yi.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shi was Jin Colonel for the Eastern Yi.

literal: His father Fang was Minister of Personnel under Murong Chui.
idiomatic: His father Fang was Minister of Personnel under Murong Chui.

literal: His elder brother Fu was Grand Marshal under Murong Chao.
idiomatic: His elder brother Fu was Grand Marshal under Murong Chao.

literal: Yi had talent and capacity and could compose writing; though Fu and he differed in conduct and length of service, their fame and rank were roughly equal.
idiomatic: Yi had talent and could write; Fu differed in conduct and tenure, yet their fame and rank were much the same.

literal: He served Murong Bao as Central Secretariat Director and Minister of the Household.
idiomatic: He served Murong Bao as Secretariat Director and Minister of the Household.

literal: When Bao was defeated he returned to Wei and was made Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Grand Master for the Imperial Commissariat, and Viscount of Zhang'an.
idiomatic: When Bao fell he entered Wei as Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Grand Master of the Imperial Commissariat, and Viscount of Zhang'an.

literal: Emperor Daowu received him in audience and asked about old Yan affairs; Yi answered with negligence and was dismissed and sent home.
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu asked about old Yan affairs; Yi answered with negligence, was dismissed, and sent home.

literal: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was again summoned and appointed Grand Master for the Imperial Commissariat; his noble rank was raised to Marquis.
idiomatic: At the start of Mingyuan he was summoned again as Grand Master of the Commissariat and raised to Marquis.

literal: He died in office.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: Yi compiled the "Book of Yan," which circulated quite widely in the world.
idiomatic: Yi compiled the Book of Yan, which circulated widely.

literal: His son Xuanzhi was executed for plotting disorder with Sima Guofan, Wen Kai, and others.
idiomatic: His son Xuanzhi was executed for plotting with Sima Guofan, Wen Kai, and others.

literal: At execution Emperor Mingyuan said to him: "In the end I will not let your line be cut off; I shall spare one of your sons."
idiomatic: At execution Emperor Mingyuan said, "I will not end your line; I spare one son."

literal: Xuanzhi, because his younger brother Qian's son Monu, styled Junming, had been orphaned early, begged to spare his life.
idiomatic: Xuanzhi begged life for his nephew Monu, styled Junming, Qian's orphaned son.

literal: They therefore killed Xuanzhi's four sons and pardoned Monu, who was punished by castration as a eunuch.
idiomatic: They killed Xuanzhi's four sons, pardoned Monu, and castrated him as a eunuch.

literal: At Cui Hao's execution Emperor Taiwu said to Monu: "You should have been spared entirely; the reason you suffered punishment was Hao."
idiomatic: At Cui Hao's fall Emperor Taiwu told Monu, "You should have been spared; Hao brought your punishment."

literal: Later he was Director of the Middle Palace Attendants, sent to Zhangye, and granted the noble rank Viscount of Fucheng.
idiomatic: Later he was Director of Palace Attendants, sent to Zhangye, and made Viscount of Fucheng.

literal: He died as Inspector of Huaizhou; posthumously he was made Duke of Bohai with the posthumous title Ding.
idiomatic: He died Inspector of Huaizhou and was posthumously Duke of Bohai, posthumous title Ding.

literal: A clansman's son Shunian was made his heir.
idiomatic: A clansman's son Shunian was made his heir.

literal: Hui, styled Shunian—Emperor Xiaowen granted the name—was a descendant of Murong Chui's Grand Marshal Yi.
idiomatic: Hui, styled Shunian—a name granted by Emperor Xiaowen—descended from Murong Chui's Grand Marshal Yi.

literal: His father Jian.
idiomatic: His father was Jian.

literal: At first, after Monu had taken Hui as heir, he requested it of Emperor Xianwen.
idiomatic: When Monu took Hui as heir he petitioned Emperor Xianwen.

literal: Jian was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Cangshui.
idiomatic: Jian was posthumously General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Cangshui.

literal: Hui inherited Monu's noble rank as Viscount of Fucheng.
idiomatic: Hui inherited Monu's rank as Viscount of Fucheng.

literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Anzhou.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he rose to Inspector of Anzhou.

literal: The mountain man Yuan Pu, father and son, lodged together and slept in one room.
idiomatic: The mountain man Yuan Pu, father and son, lodged and slept in one room.

literal: When Hui took office he ordered them to lodge separately and the custom there changed.
idiomatic: Hui on taking office ordered separate lodging and the custom changed.

literal: Under Emperor Ming he was Inspector of Yingzhou.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was Inspector of Yingzhou.

literal: At that time, after the disorders of the Mahayana sect and in addition floods, he memorialized asking relief and exemption from military levies; the province relied on him.
idiomatic: After Mahayana rebellion and floods he sought relief and exemption from levies; the province relied on him.

literal: He served as Minister of Revenue, Minister of Justice, and Grand Rectifier of Jizhou.
idiomatic: He served as Minister of Revenue, Minister of Justice, and Grand Rectifier of Jizhou.

literal: Zheng Yun of Xingyang curried favor with the Director of the Long Autumn Office Liu Teng and with four hundred bolts of purple gauze bought the post of Inspector of Anzhou.
idiomatic: Zheng Yun of Xingyang fawned on Liu Teng of the Long Autumn Office and bought Inspector of Anzhou with four hundred bolts of purple gauze.

literal: The appointment letter came out in the morning; in the evening he went to call on Hui, and before he had sat down he asked Hui: "In Anzhou, what line of business is most profitable?"
idiomatic: The appointment came at dawn; that evening he called on Hui and, before sitting, asked what business paid best in Anzhou.

literal: Hui said: "You bear the state's favor and have reached a frontier post; though you cannot uproot the mallow in your garden or send away the weaving woman, you ought to think of plans to aid the people—why come on your first visit to ask about business?"
idiomatic: Hui said, "You bear the state's grace and hold a frontier post; though you cannot uproot your mallows or send away your weaver, you should aid the people—why on your first visit ask about profit?"

literal: Feng Hui is no merchant—why show me this?"
idiomatic: Feng Hui is no merchant—why show me this?"

literal: Yun flushed and lost color.
idiomatic: Yun flushed pale.

literal: Transferred to Minister of the Seven Armies while holding the post of Imperial Censor; he impeached the Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yuan Qin for adultery with his cousin Li's wife Cui; men of the time praised him.
idiomatic: Made Minister of the Seven Armies and Imperial Censor; he impeached Vice Minister Yuan Qin for adultery with his cousin's wife Cui, and men praised him.

literal: Later he was Minister in the Palace, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
idiomatic: Later he was Palace Minister and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

literal: Posthumously he was made Duke of the Ministry of Works with the posthumous title Xiaoxuan.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was Duke of Works, posthumous title Xiaoxuan.

literal: His eldest son was Longzhi.
idiomatic: His eldest son was Longzhi.

literal: Longzhi, styled Zuyi, childhood name Pi, was generous and had measure.
idiomatic: Longzhi, styled Zuyi, childhood name Pi, was generous and measured.

literal: In the Yanchang era the monk Faqing made disorder in Jizhou, styled himself Mahayana, and had fifty thousand followers.
idiomatic: In Yanchang the monk Faqing rebelled in Jizhou, styled himself Mahayana, and gathered fifty thousand men.

literal: Longzhi as Colonel of Army Affairs in the Opening Office joined the Grand Commander Yuan Yao in suppressing him.
idiomatic: Longzhi as Opening Office colonel joined Grand Commander Yuan Yao to suppress him.

literal: Faqing was captured and Longzhi was granted the noble rank Viscount of Wucheng.
idiomatic: Faqing was taken and Longzhi made Viscount of Wucheng.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Henei.
idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Henei.

literal: Before he reached the commandery, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Emperor Zhuang was imprisoned and died; Longzhi, because his father had been killed, constantly harbored revenge and, holding the staff of office, went east to plot a righteous rising.
idiomatic: Before he took the post Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Emperor Zhuang died in prison; Longzhi, his father slain, held the staff and went east to plot revenge.

literal: He joined Gao Gan and others in a night attack on Jizhou, took it, and was thereupon pushed as Inspector.
idiomatic: He joined Gao Gan in a night attack on Jizhou, took it, and was pushed as Inspector.

literal: When Qi Prince Shenwu marched east from Jinyang, Longzhi sent his son Zihui with Gao Gan to welcome him at Fukou.
idiomatic: When Prince Shenwu marched east from Jinyang, Longzhi sent Zihui with Gao Gan to welcome him at Fukou.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made Minister of Personnel.
idiomatic: At the start of Zhongxing he was Minister of Personnel.

literal: At the battle of Hanling he remained to guard Ye.
idiomatic: At Hanling he stayed to guard Ye.

literal: Before long he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Duke of Ande Commandery.
idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed Duke of Ande.

literal: At that time court opinion held that Erzhu Rong should receive sacrifice in Emperor Ming's temple hall.
idiomatic: Court opinion then held Erzhu Rong should share sacrifice in Emperor Ming's temple.

literal: Longzhi argued: "Rong was a subject who personally carried out murder and treason—how can there be reason for a man who harmed another's mother to share food with her son?"
idiomatic: Longzhi argued, "Rong was a subject who murdered his lord—how can a man who killed a mother dine with her son?"

literal: Because he took part in deliberating the new regulations of the Unicorn Toe Office, his wife's clan the Zu were also enfeoffed as Lady of Fanyang Commandery.
idiomatic: Deliberating new regulations at the Unicorn Toe Office, he also enfeoffed his wife's clan Zu as Lady of Fanyang.

literal: Longzhi memorialized to transfer his former ranks as Viscount of Fucheng and Viscount of Wucheng to his nephews Xiaowan and others; the court approved and followed his wish.
idiomatic: Longzhi memorialized to transfer his ranks Fucheng and Wucheng to nephews Xiaowan and others; the court approved.

literal: Later he was framed by Huasi Chun and others, fled to his home village, and Prince Shenwu summoned him to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Later Huasi Chun framed him; he fled home and Prince Shenwu summoned him to Jinyang.

literal: When Emperor Xiaojing of Wei was established he was made Minister of Personnel and soon added Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojing was established he was Minister of Personnel and soon Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he was made Inspector of Jizhou with the Opening Office; he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: In Yuanxiang 1 he was Inspector of Jizhou with Opening Office rank and rose to Right Vice Minister.

literal: When Gao Zhongmi, Northern Prefect of Yuzhou, was about to rebel he secretly won the great families of Jizhou as inside allies.
idiomatic: When Northern Yuzhou Prefect Gao Zhongmi was about to rebel he secretly won Jizhou magnates as allies within.

literal: An edict ordered Longzhi to gallop on post-horses to comfort and soothe them, and the region was thereby quieted.
idiomatic: An edict sent Longzhi on post-horses to soothe them and the region quieted.

literal: Longzhi from the first took part in Prince Shenwu's strategy; every subtle plan he reported in secret; he cut drafts by hand and few outside knew.
idiomatic: Longzhi had shared Prince Shenwu's strategy from the start; subtle plans he reported in secret, cutting drafts by hand that few outside knew.

literal: He died as Inspector of Qizhou; posthumously he was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He died Inspector of Qizhou and was posthumously Minister of Works.

literal: Prince Shenwu, because posthumous honor was not yet complete, again petitioned to grant Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Xuanyi.
idiomatic: Prince Shenwu, finding honor incomplete, petitioned again for Grand Tutor, posthumous title Xuanyi.

literal: When the Prince later reached the northern border of Jizhou and stopped at Jiaojin Ford he recalled Longzhi, turned to the acting prefect Sima Ziru, spoke of his virtue, and wept for him.
idiomatic: Later at Jizhou's northern border, Jiaojin Ford, the Prince recalled Longzhi, told Sima Ziru of his virtue, and wept.

literal: He ordered a second grand sacrifice sent to offer sacrifice.
idiomatic: He ordered a grand second sacrifice sent.

literal: Longzhi served five emperors and was known for cautious plainness.
idiomatic: Longzhi served five emperors and was known for plain caution.

literal: In all he was Attendant-in-Ordinary four times, Minister of Personnel twice, Vice Minister once, and Inspector of Jizhou four times.
idiomatic: Four times Attendant-in-Ordinary, twice Minister of Personnel, once Vice Minister, four times Inspector of Jizhou.

literal: Each time he came to Jizhou the old men of the province all said: "Our Lord Feng has come again."
idiomatic: Each arrival in Jizhou the old men said, "Our Lord Feng has come again."

literal: Such was the hold he had on men's hearts.
idiomatic: Such was the hold he had on hearts.

literal: His son Zihui inherited.
idiomatic: His son Zihui inherited.

literal: Zihui, styled Zhongzao, childhood name Sao.
idiomatic: Zihui, styled Zhongzao, childhood name Sao.

literal: His nature was harmonious and principled and he had capacity and bearing.
idiomatic: He was harmonious, principled, and had capacity.

literal: Leaving the purple he was Secretariat Clerk and was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Pingyang with the added title Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He began as Secretariat Clerk, rose to Administrator of Pingyang with Regular Attendant rank.

literal: On Jinzhou's northern border Mount Huo was oldly called the Thousand-Li Path; the mountain slopes were high and steep and whenever a great army passed, men and horses were worn with labor.
idiomatic: On Jinzhou's north Mount Huo was called the Thousand-Li Path; slopes were steep and every great army wore men and horses down.

literal: Zihui asked to open a separate road east of the valley of the old path.
idiomatic: Zihui asked to open a new road east of the old valley path.

literal: The Prince agreed and still ordered Zihui to open and repair it; in ten days it was done.
idiomatic: The Prince agreed and ordered Zihui to open it; in ten days it was done.

literal: He was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Great Office.
idiomatic: He was summoned as Director in the Great Office Ministry of Personnel.

literal: When the Prince died the secret was not yet announced; Wenxiang made Zihui Administrator of Bohai.
idiomatic: When the Prince died the death was not yet announced; Wenxiang made Zihui Administrator of Bohai.

literal: He grasped his hand and said: "I truly know this does not match a meritorious minister's standing, but you must pacify and soothe.
idiomatic: He took his hand and said, "I know this does not match your merit, but you must pacify the land.

literal: Moreover to clothe brocade and roam by day is what ancients prized; you should govern well and need not practice like an ordinary prefect going to the province for audience."
idiomatic: To clothe brocade and roam by day ancients prized; govern well and need not act like a common prefect at provincial audience."

literal: He was still permitted to gather a thousand men of his household troops.
idiomatic: He was still allowed to gather a thousand household troops.

literal: In the third year of Daning he was Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: In Daning 3 he was Minister of Justice.

literal: When Gao Guiyan rebelled he was ordered to take part in planning the military affair.
idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan rebelled he was ordered to plan the campaign.

literal: When the rebels were pacified he was ordered to act temporarily in provincial affairs.
idiomatic: When rebels were pacified he was ordered to act in provincial affairs.

literal: He was summoned as Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was summoned Equal to the Three Dukes and Right Vice Minister.

literal: When he died his posthumous title was Jian.
idiomatic: At death his posthumous title was Jian.

literal: His son Baogai inherited.
idiomatic: His son Baogai inherited.

literal: Zihui's nephew Xiu held the post of Inspector of Huozhou.
idiomatic: Zihui's nephew Xiu was Inspector of Huozhou.

literal: When the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan, Xiu's city fell and he was sent to Yangzhou.
idiomatic: When Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan, Xiu's city fell and he was sent to Yangzhou.

literal: After Qi perished he escaped and returned.
idiomatic: After Qi's fall he escaped home.

literal: He ended as Inspector of Tongzhou.
idiomatic: He ended as Inspector of Tongzhou.

literal: Xiu's outward appearance was refined and Confucian, yet his spirit was hard to offend.
idiomatic: Xiu looked refined and Confucian, yet his spirit was hard to offend.

literal: His elder sister's husband, Minister of Works Lou Dingyuan, was Inspector of Yingzhou; Xiu was Administrator of Bohai.
idiomatic: His sister's husband, Minister Lou Dingyuan, was Inspector of Yingzhou; Xiu was Administrator of Bohai.
